raw.assessment: The incumbent produced the intended course set in 32/40 exports (80%) with median handling of 17 minutes, missing both targets. Its strongest supported account is that routine exports can work well, while change-related cases concentrate difficulties: 24 unchanged-assignment files had median handling of seven minutes, a concrete counterexample to uniformly burdensome processing; six affected exports involved assignment changes and two renames. Mutable assignment/name interpretation is a hypothesis, not an observed cause. Replacement delays greatly exceed job runtime, but waiting cannot be equated with measured handling. No sampled cross-center rows supports only this sample; the omitted course-split center limits coverage.

openings.claim: Resolving the requested week's courses through current assignments or mutable names may misidentify courses after reassignment or renaming.
openings.delta: Test historical course identity and membership before changing export scheduling or execution speed.
openings.prediction: With identical intended course sets, reassignment or renaming changes incumbent selection; a week-specific identity mapping removes those differences. No such differences would weaken this account.
openings.probe: In private staging, compare fabricated unchanged, reassigned, renamed and split-course fixtures against explicit expected center/week/course IDs. Compare incumbent selection with a minimal week-specific mapping; verify documented CSV import, zero foreign-center rows and concurrent attendance entry. Estimate history availability, effort and hosting cost before implementation.
assumptions: Course identities and relevant historical membership can be reconstructed.
A production correction must fit six engineer-days and existing hosting; feasibility is unproven.

openings.claim: How much apparent omission reflects disagreement between coordinators' timetables and the service about the intended course set?
openings.delta: Distinguish selection defects from differences in expected membership that a query correction alone would not resolve.
openings.prediction: Expectation mismatch produces disagreement before export inspection; selection defects produce missing agreed course IDs after expectations align.
openings.probe: Across the six coordinators' two short sessions, privately record intended course IDs and timetable update times before showing exports, then reconcile disagreements against dated changes. Use fabricated participants and record checking versus import time separately.
assumptions: Coordinators can identify dated schedule changes.
Six volunteers may not represent all eight centers.

raw.assessment: The supplied synthetic baseline misses both course-set and handling-time targets. Assignment changes and renames are associated with affected exports, but causation is unestablished. No observed cross-center rows in this sample establishes neither isolation for course splits nor future safety.

openings.claim: Speculative capability: a private, week-addressable export recipe that retains the intended course identities through instructor changes and renames, and requires an explicit decision for course splits.
openings.delta: Course selection would depend on dated course identity rather than current instructor assignment. Full capability needs stable center-scoped identifiers, reliable effective dates, rename/split lineage, an authoritative intended-course set, and a consistent read while attendance entry continues. Presently testable fragment: a coordinator-approved center/week course-ID manifest driving the existing CSV serializer on fabricated staging data.
openings.prediction: If current-assignment selection causes omissions, changing an instructor or course label without changing intended membership will alter incumbent coverage but leave manifest-driven coverage correct.
openings.probe: Replay paired fabricated fixtures differing only in assignment or label; separately exercise a split with explicit intended membership. Compare both exporters against the approved set and seed foreign-center sentinel participants. Check documented CSV import and simultaneous attendance writes. Scope implementation before proceeding; retain the six-day and hosting limits.
assumptions: Stable identifiers and nonblocking reads exist or fit the bounded change.
Coordinators can agree the intended set; conflicting timetable evidence must remain unresolved until reconciled.

openings.claim: Does checking course coverage dominate handling time even when the CSV already contains the correct records?
openings.delta: Distinguishes verification burden from downloading/importing work, which completion logs cannot reveal.
openings.prediction: If checking dominates, a private course/week coverage preview should reduce checking time on correct files while leaving import time similar; import-dominated handling predicts little total improvement.
openings.probe: Use six coordinators' two short sessions for counterbalanced, matched fabricated correct-file tasks with and without a staging preview. Time checking, correcting, downloading and importing separately, excluding replacement waiting. Record coverage mistakes as well as time; treat results as exploratory, not proof of next-40 success.
assumptions: A small private preview fits existing resources.
Fabricated tasks approximate routine work sufficiently to identify a bottleneck.

openings.claim: Current assignments/names may corrupt historical selection; test an approved center/week course-ID manifest.
openings.discriminator: Assignment/name-only changes alter incumbent coverage, not manifest coverage.
openings.fit: Uncertain: private processing, documented CSV, six days/existing hosting, uninterrupted attendance entry.
openings.probe: Replay unchanged/reassigned/renamed and explicitly decided split fixtures; compare agreed coverage; check foreign-center sentinels, CSV import, concurrent writes; estimate implementation.
openings.uncertainty: Association only. Needs stable center-scoped IDs, reconstructable history/effective dates, rename/split lineage, authoritative membership and consistent nonblocking reads.

openings.claim: Timetable disagreement may explain apparent omissions independently.
openings.discriminator: Disagreement before inspection versus agreed IDs missing afterward.
openings.fit: Preserves constraints through private fabricated tasks.
openings.probe: Elicit intended IDs/update times before exports; reconcile dated changes; separate checking/import time.
openings.uncertainty: Dated evidence may be missing; preserve unresolved conflicts; six volunteers may not represent eight centers.

openings.claim: Coverage checking may dominate handling of correct files.
openings.discriminator: Preview reduces checking with similar import time; import dominance predicts little benefit.
openings.fit: Preserves if small private preview fits resources; retain CSV.
openings.probe: Counterbalance fabricated correct-file tasks with/without preview; time checking/correction/download/import, record errors; exclude replacement waiting.
openings.uncertainty: Preview feasibility/task realism unproven; exploratory results cannot establish next-40 success.

lineage.reason: With Z1: manifest, splits, dependencies preserved.

post_distill.decision: Prioritize membership/selection probes; share six coordinators' two sessions across D2/D3. Synthetic baseline 80%/17 minutes; unchanged-assignment median seven. Next-40 targets: 95%, <=12 minutes, zero foreign rows. Omitted split center limits isolation evidence.
